troubleshooting.title: Deliveries fail or stay in retrying
troubleshooting.shortdesc: Events reach the relay, but your application doesn’t get them, or gets them late. Start with lattice deliveries show on one affected delivery: its last attempt names the cause in almost every case. Fictional sample written for this portfolio.

ul.li: lattice deliveries list shows deliveries in the state retrying for more than a few minutes, or in failed.
The sender reports 401 Unauthorized from the relay’s address.
Your application receives the same event twice.

strow.stentry: The target address is wrong, the target is down, or a firewall in front of it doesn’t allow the relay’s addresses.
The target is overloaded or restarting. The relay retries these on its own.
The target expects a credential the relay doesn’t send.
signature mismatch on an attempt to your target
Your application verifies Relay-Signature with a different secret from the one the relay signs with.
rejected: signature mismatch on the incoming event
The secret in RELAY_SOURCE_SECRET differs from the one the sender signs with, or the sender signs a different header.
The target took longer than timeout_seconds to answer the first time, so the relay sent it again.

step.cmd: From a machine outside your network, request the target’s address with curl -i. If it fails there too, the problem is the target, not the relay.
If it succeeds, allow the relay’s outbound addresses in your firewall. lattice info lists them for your region.
Replay one delivery, and then watch it.

info.codeblock: lattice deliveries replay <delivery id> lattice deliveries show <delivery id>

step.cmd: Add the credential the target expects as a header in relay.yaml, with the value in an environment variable.

info.codeblock: targets: - name: app url_from: RELAY_TARGET_URL headers: Authorization: "Bearer ${RELAY_TARGET_TOKEN}"

step.cmd: Set the variable, and then deploy again.

info.codeblock: lattice env set RELAY_TARGET_TOKEN=<the token your application expects> lattice deploy

step.cmd: Confirm which secret each side uses. The relay verifies incoming events with RELAY_SOURCE_SECRET, and signs outgoing deliveries with the project’s delivery secret, shown once under Settings > Signing in the console.
In your application, verify Relay-Signature with the delivery secret, not with the sender’s secret. The two are different on purpose, so that a leaked sender secret can’t forge deliveries.
Compute the signature over the raw request body, before any JSON parsing. A parser that reorders keys changes the bytes.
Make your handler idempotent: store Relay-Delivery-Id and ignore an id you have already processed.
Answer 202 as soon as you have stored the event, and do the work afterwards. A target that answers within a second is never retried for a timeout.
If the work can’t be deferred, raise timeout_seconds to at most 30.

remedy.title: If none of this fixes it

steps-informal.p: Collect the delivery id, the output of lattice deliveries show, and the time of the attempt in UTC. Open a ticket with the Lattice Relay support team from the console’s Help menu, and include the three items. The team can see the relay’s side of each attempt but not your target’s logs, so attach those too.
